authoring_note: Supplied-DATA event-schema / relation-frame library, authored from GENERAL Schank-Abelson script knowledge (script theory: application of a known event schema with expected roles/preconditions/outcomes) and Trabasso-style goal-plan story-grammar categories (goal / attempt / outcome, satisfy / thwart / enable-cause links). Authored BEFORE reverse-engineering from the specific gold link text -- each schema names a GENERAL narrative situation type (prohibition-reconciliation, rescue-gratitude, sacrifice-for-other, confession-under-confinement, illness-caretaking, financial-shock, diagnosis-life-decision, mistaken-identity-adoption, etc.) that recurs across many stories, not a paraphrase of a specific Anne-of-Green-Gables sentence. Two CONTROL schemas (GET_DRESSED_SCRIPT, RESTAURANT_SCRIPT) are canonical Schank illustrations included specifically to demonstrate general-script authorship discipline; they are NOT expected to fire on this text and any fire on them is a genuine false positive.

schemas.note: An authority figure forbids an association/behavior (the unstated goal behind the prohibition speech act is 'stop/prevent the behavior'); later a reconciliation event restores it.
A character rescues/saves another from danger or illness (unstated goal: save/help); the rescued party's family later expresses gratitude, which may unlock a prior prohibition.
An agent withdraws/gives up something valuable so a DIFFERENT agent can have it instead (satisfy = the other agent completes the desire the sacrifice was FOR).
A confined/punished character confesses (unstated goal: end the confinement/be freed); satisfy = release or forgiveness restoring freedom.
A character pleads on behalf of a third party who is at risk of losing a privilege (unstated goal: spare the third party); satisfy = privilege restored.
Someone falls ill with no adult present; a competent bystander acts (unstated goal: cure/help); satisfy = recovery followed by gratitude.
An enabling-precondition CAUSE frame: an early warning/worry about a risk precedes a later calamity that realizes it -- no goal mediation, pure enabling cause.
A medical diagnosis/prognosis is the enabling precondition for a subsequent major life-course decision.
News of financial ruin is the enabling precondition for a physiological shock reaction.
A THWART frame: a persisting grudge/resentment is the cause that overrides/thwarts what would otherwise be a gratitude-satisfy response.
An authority demands an apology (unstated/explicit goal: compliance); satisfy = the apology is accepted / forgiveness granted.
An accidental substitution/mixup is the enabling cause of an embarrassing or punitive consequence.
A character secretly decides to buy/make something for a loved one (unstated goal: please/surprise them); satisfy = the gift is delivered as requested.

An authority deliberately imposes a frightening/unpleasant experience as a corrective lesson (unstated goal: correct the child's behavior/belief) -- a CONTROL-leaning schema, no expected reconciliation satisfy event.
An enabling-precondition CAUSE frame: an offered opportunity/extra instruction enables a later competitive achievement.
A character states a standing wish/request; much later, unprompted by any intervening event, the request is finally granted (persisting-state cause, not proximate re-trigger).
An enabling-precondition CAUSE frame: a mix-up in who was sent/expected leads to a downstream adoption/practical-arrangement decision.
An enabling-precondition CAUSE frame: an invented imaginative game/story is taken seriously enough by its author to require a corrective real-world intervention.

schemas.note: A THWART frame variant: an old, specific grievance persists unresolved across a long time-gap and is the direct (non-superseded) cause of a much-later refusal.
An enabling-precondition CAUSE frame: an irreversible physical mishap (a color/substance that will not wash out or undo) forces a specific remedial action.
